The fear of prolonged bed rest keeps many patients from getting timely medical help for their back pain. A common worry is that a major operation means staying stuck in bed for months without moving. Fortunately, modern medical techniques have changed things completely. Early movement is actually the secret to a fast and safe recovery.

Getting back on your feet quickly prevents blood clots, keeps your muscles from getting stiff, and helps your lungs function much better. However, moving too early or sitting incorrectly can place unwanted pressure on your healing back. If you are experiencing chronic spinal pain and want to explore safe treatment options, scheduling a personalised assessment with an experienced spine specialist in Ahmedabad at Silver Touch Hospitals will help clarify your specific recovery timeline.

Walking Safely After Your Surgery

For minor or minimally invasive procedures, like a simple microdiscectomy, walking begins incredibly fast. Most patients are encouraged to stand up and take short, assisted walks within 24 hours of their operation.

In case you have undergone a more intricate surgery like spinal fusion, you may need to give yourself some extra days of rest before being ready for your first walk. The nursing staff or physiotherapists will be at your side, assisting you during the beginning stages of your first walk. The most important thing is to begin walking for only five minutes and slowly increase the distance covered. During this period, you should totally refrain from flexing the spine, twisting the waist, or carrying loads.

Here’s a breakdown:

  • Day 1 After Surgery ──► Stand up and take short, assisted walks
  • Week 1 to Week 2 ──► Walk 5-10 minutes multiple times a day
  • Week 3 to Week 6 ──► Gradually increase to comfortable outdoor walks

Safe Sitting Guidelines to Protect Your Back

Sitting actually puts more mechanical pressure on your lower spine than standing or lying flat. For the first two to three weeks, you should strictly limit your sitting time to short intervals of fifteen to twenty minutes per session.

When you do sit down, choose a firm chair with a straight back and proper armrests. Your knees should stay at the same level as your hips, and your feet must rest completely flat on the ground. You must avoid deep, soft sofas or low plastic stools because they force your back to curve outwards.
